speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked	the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what is the number of Long-Term Visit Pass Plus (LTVP+) granted after 30 September 2014; and (b) what are the annual number and percentage of unsuccessful LTVP+ applications since LTVP+ was introduced.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Long-Term Visit Pass Plus (LTVP+) was introduced on 1 April 2012 as an enhancement to the Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP) scheme.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The LTVP+ grants long-term stay to foreign spouses of Singaporeans whose marriages have been stable over time.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There is no separate application process for LTVP+.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Singaporeans can apply for LTVP or LTVP+ for their foreign spouses through the same process.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Foreign spouses who meet the criteria will be granted LTVP+.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Those who do not meet the LTVP+ criteria but meet the LTVP criteria would be granted LTVP.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There may be a number of reasons why an application is unsuccessful.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These include the ability of the Singaporean spouse to support the family financially, or the length of marriage.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are there plans to increase any benefit for LTVP+?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I understand that they are also not counted as part of the foreign worker quota for employers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: They are not currently counted as part of the foreign worker quota requirement if they successfully apply for the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) Letter of Consent.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: There are no immediate plans to increase the benefits of the LTVP+ holders.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: LTVP+ holders currently enjoy a greater certainty of stay here, with longer periods of residency compared to LTVP holders.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The employers are also not required to pay the foreign worker levy for them.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: The second question is: should they encounter rejections from employers who say that they cannot employ them, even with a Letter of Consent, notwithstanding other possible reasons, what should they do?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Because one of the feedback has been that employers still consider them as foreign workers and say that it is really troublesome to hire them.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: That is not very helpful when they are also trying to work to supplement their household income and working towards gaining PR status so that their citizen families – generally, the majority are citizen families – can stay intact and remain stable in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: From the policy point of view, it is very clear that once the person is given the Letter of Consent, he or she is not counted as part of the foreign worker quota and there is no levy imposed on the foreign workers with LTVP or LTVP+.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As to why they are not employed, there could be plenty of reasons.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: It is important to highlight specific cases to MOM for further investigation.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have a question regarding the application process for LTVP and LTVP+.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For applicants, for example, who have Singaporean children – one or two children or even more – are they regarded any differently in terms of the application process?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is the process, perhaps, expedited for such situations?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I ask because I have seen quite a few families, where the father is a citizen and the child is a citizen, and the mother had been trying but had not been able to get an LTVP.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could the Parliamentary Secretary shed some light on this, please?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Applications for LTVP+ are considered holistically based on a range of factors.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: These include the duration of the marriage and whether the couple have children from the marriage and the ability of the Singaporean sponsor to support the family.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: It is difficult to give the Member an assurance that once you have children, you will automatically get an LTVP.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The point is that it is a whole basket of factors that needs to be considered.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Coming back to the question of the "unsuccessful rate", the Parliamentary Secretary just mentioned about the financial capability of the spouse.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Besides that, are there any other major reasons for the rejection?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: There are many factors and they include also whether there are any adverse records of the person applying for an LTVP and, as I have mentioned, it includes the ability to support as well as the stability of the marriage.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Just a couple of supplementary questions for the Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I understand that one of the criteria for granting an LTVP+ is whether the marriage is stable.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: If that could be spelt out, it would provide a lot of certainty to the entire family.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My other question is a suggestion for the Parliamentary Secretary to consider: if there is such a criterion, whether attempts could be made so that for those who have met that criterion are automatically upgraded from LTVP to LTVP+, without the need to apply.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: It is not a very easy thing to define how stable the marriage is.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But there are also various factors including the record of the applicant who is applying, in terms of how many times he or she had been married.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As for the second question, it is currently in the same process.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: So, if they qualify for LTVP+, they will be given LTVP+.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I just wonder if the Ministry could share this with the applicants as well because I have seen the rejection letter and it just says, "The application is rejected." For example, if it is a financial consideration, then maybe that is something that the applicant's spouse can do to increase the salary.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When we just say, "It is rejected", it is hard for us to write the appeal letter and hard for the applicants as well.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I will take it up with the Ministry.
